I was born in 1980's, so I grew up in the era when PC games like this were a big deal. When Age of Empires II first came out in 1999, I was 16. Back then, this was the kind of game you could lose an entire afternoon to without even noticing. Build your little town, send villagers to collect resources, age up, build an army, and somehow end up spending way too much time trying to take down that one enemy castle.

Fast-forward to today, and here I am playing it again on an old laptop with an i7-4800MQ, 16 GB of RAM and a GeForce GT 730M. Honestly, I'm surprised it even runs on this thing, but here we are! That's pretty impressive for a game with this much content.

And the amount of content is just ridiculous. So many campaigns, so many historical figures, so many stories to play through. Joan of Arc, William Wallace, Saladin, Genghis Khan... there's always another campaign waiting for you. You can play for hours and still feel like there's plenty left to explore.

And that soundtrack! If you know, you know. Just hearing those tunes brings back memories. It's one of those soundtracks that gets stuck in your head, in the best possible way.

Sure, the graphics have aged, but who cares? The gameplay is still great, the campaigns are genuinely fun, and there's something satisfying about building an empire from scratch and watching it all come together.

Some games are fun for a few years and then you move on. Age of Empires II is one of those games you can come back to decades later and still have a blast.

I play Age of Empires II on an AMD gaming computer with an RTX 5070 and 32GB of RAM. 
My name is Marcus Halberstram.
I'm 27 years old.

I believe in taking care of my villagers, in a balanced economy, and a rigorous Dark-age routine.
In the beginning, I build 2 houses. I'll send a villager to lure a boar while doing my stomach crunches.
I can do a thousand now.

While they kill the boar, I make a lumbermill and gather 6 sheep.
As I queue more villagers, I send my scout to look for relics. 
Then a mill near my honey-almond berry farm.
And on the edge of my gold, a palisade wall.

I then build a barracks and stable, which I leave as part of my wall while I prepare the rest of my routine.
I always wall-off using houses and little-to-no palisade walls, because walls use up your wood and make you look like a noob. Then more villagers, then a few more houses, followed by advancing to the feudal age.

There is an idea of a perfect Dark-age.
Some kind of abstraction, but there is no perfect age.
Only an entity-- something illusory.
And though I can hide my cold gaze...
and you can shake my hand and feel flesh gripping yours...
and maybe you can even sense our playstyles are probably comparable,
I simply...am not there.
